About Me

I'm a Mechanical Engineering student at ANITS who builds backend systems and AI/computer vision software. During my internship at APTRANSCO, I engineered an end-to-end AI drone inspection system in Django and PostgreSQL, integrating custom YOLO models that reached 92% mAP. Outside that, I've built and deployed three other full-stack platforms — a real-time bus tracking system, a lab automation tool, and a flowchart builder. I enjoy building production-ready backend systems rather than academic prototypes.

APTRANSCO Transmission Inspection System
Production ProjectInternship2026Govt. of Andhra Pradesh
Live Demo ↗ Architecture Source ↗
Overview

An end-to-end platform that takes a drone flight — RGB and thermal footage, GPS-logged — through a ten-stage pipeline of detection, segmentation, thermal analysis, and change tracking, and out the other side as a real-time dashboard, an auto-generated PDF report, and a routed maintenance alert. Running 10 AI detection models across defect, vegetation, and wildlife-risk categories.

YOLO24SAM 3.1OpenCV DINOv2SSIMChart.js ReportLabFlutterDjango PostgreSQLDocker
Problem

Manual review couldn't keep up with drone-scale data.

Scale

APTRANSCO inspects thousands of transmission towers across the state.

Cost & Speed

Manual patrol-based inspection is slow and resource-intensive.

Volume

Each batch mission processes dozens of images per tower across multiple towers.

Review Bottleneck

Reviewing every image manually, tower by tower, is impractical at this scale.

Solution & Architecture

A ten-stage pipeline, from drone dispatch to maintenance alert.

Hover a stage for what it actually does.

01
Drone Flight Dispatch
RGB + thermal capture, with GPS logging.
02
Data Upload to System
Images, video, and thermal scans stored.
03
YOLO24 Defect Detection
Bounding boxes and confidence scores.
04
SAM 3.1 Segmentation
Pixel-level damage isolation.
05
Thermal Hotspot Analysis
OpenCV thresholding and thermal color mapping.
06
Historical Comparison
DINOv2 embeddings + SSIM change detection.
07
Predictive Analytics
Risk score and failure probability.
08
Dashboard Auto-Update
Real-time display via Chart.js.
09
PDF Report Generation
ReportLab — defect images and recommendations.
10
Maintenance Alert Dispatch
Auto-routed to the right team with an SLA.

Challenges

Label consistency — solved with a written labeling guide and spot audits.

False positives — solved with hard-negative mining and threshold tuning.

GPU limitations — solved by staging experiments as smaller, iterative runs.

Legacy infra gaps — replaced ngrok/debug signing with a proper domain and release build.

Enterprise Real-Time Bus Tracking Platform
Personal ProjectShipped & Used
Watch Demo Source ↗
Overview

A multi-role platform (admin / driver / student) with JWT-based access control, supporting 100+ concurrent users. Delivered sub-200ms GPS update latency using Django Channels (WebSockets) for bidirectional real-time communication, with 10+ RESTful APIs built on DRF, plus a companion React Native driver app for live location streaming, trip lifecycle management, and issue reporting.

DjangoDjango REST FrameworkDjango Channels (WebSockets) JWT AuthReact NativeJavaScriptPostgreSQL

Architecture

Three roles, one real-time channel.

01
JWT-Based Access Control
Admin, driver, and student roles authenticate separately.

Driver App Streams Live GPS

03
Django Channels (WebSockets)

10+ REST APIs (DRF)

Features

What it actually does.

Multi-role access

Separate admin, driver, and student roles with JWT-based auth.

Real-time GPS sync

Sub-200ms location updates via Django Channels WebSockets.

Trip lifecycle management

Drivers manage trips start-to-finish from the React Native app.

Issue reporting

Drivers can report issues directly from the field.

Lessons

What this project taught me.

Real-time is different

WebSocket-based systems need different thinking than request/response APIs.

Auth at scale

Role-based JWT auth across three user types taught me proper access control design.

Confidence for what came next

This project is what made the APTRANSCO internship possible.
